lines.japanese: きんと冷えた朝を泳ぐ。
lines.english: I swam through the keen chill of morning.

lines.japanese: 現代建築芸術の展覧会みたいな通学路。僕の両脇には、車道を挟んで、先鋭的なデザインの一戸建てやマンションが隙間なく並んでいる。
lines.english: My route to school resembled an exhibition of modern architectural art. On either side of the road, houses and apartment buildings in daring modern designs stood packed together without a gap.

lines.japanese: ネットで見るに、この辺りは世間的にも、ハイソなイメージの住宅街として認識されているらしい。
lines.english: From what I had seen online, the neighborhood was generally regarded as an upscale residential district.

lines.japanese: でも羽田の家──訂正、僕らの家──に限っては、周囲のリフォームブームに倣わず、本邦の伝統様式に則った昔ながらのデザインそのままだった。
lines.english: The Haneda house—correction, our house—was the exception. It had resisted the remodeling fever around it and retained its old-fashioned design in the traditional Japanese style.

lines.japanese: 長らく団地住まいだった羽田家が、中古ながら念願のマイホームを手に入れたのは、僕が美空学園に入学する直前。
lines.english: The Haneda family had lived in apartment complexes for years. We finally acquired the long-desired home of our own, secondhand though it was, just before I entered Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: 広さではわりと誇れる家だけど、叔母さんはご近所の未来ハウスに対して少なからず劣等感があるらしい。
lines.english: Its size was something we could take a certain pride in, but my aunt seemed to harbor a substantial inferiority complex toward the futuristic houses around us.

lines.japanese: 駅までの道のりは、朝特有の早足で徒歩十分。
lines.english: The station was ten minutes away at the brisk pace peculiar to morning.

lines.japanese: 目指す先を望めば、楚々と並んだ屋根の山脈の向こうに、スーパーマーケットの四角い屋上広告塔が見える。朱色の箱に、翼を広げた白い野鳥のシルエット。
lines.english: Ahead of me, beyond a mountain range of neatly aligned roofs, rose the square rooftop sign of a supermarket: a white wild bird, wings outspread, against a vermilion box.

lines.japanese: 年老いた鳥は遠く高度経済成長期の時世から、長らく風見ヶ丘駅前の道標として住人たちの灯台代わりを務めてきた。
lines.english: Ever since the distant years of rapid economic growth, that aging bird had served the residents as a lighthouse and a marker pointing the way to Kazamigaoka Station.

lines.japanese: だけどその座は、より天空へ近いアーキテクチャーの出現によって、一年前にあっさり奪われた。
lines.english: But a new work of architecture, closer to the heavens, had casually usurped its place a year ago.

lines.japanese: 風見ヶ丘の新たなシンボルは、駅前の一等地に近隣住人の反対を押しきって生えた超高層マンション。
lines.english: Kazamigaoka’s new symbol was a high-rise condominium that had sprouted on prime land before the station despite the opposition of local residents.

lines.japanese: 地上３０階……４０階だったかな。いいや。立ちどまって窓を数えてたら電車を一本逃すかもしれない。
lines.english: Thirty stories tall… Or was it forty? Never mind. If I stopped to count the windows, I might miss a train.

lines.japanese: あそこに住んでいるひと達は、来る日も来る日もふもとの僕らに眺望されていることを知っているのだろうか。
lines.english: Did the people who lived up there know that, day after day, all of us at the foot of their tower gazed up at them?

lines.japanese: はるか高みを見上げながら角をひとつ曲がったとき、不意に僕の視点は地べたに引きもどされた。水色のスモッグを着た小さな女の子が、アスファルトの上でうつ伏せになって泣いていた。
lines.english: I rounded a corner with my eyes still raised to those distant heights, and suddenly my attention was dragged back to earth. A little girl in a pale blue smock lay facedown on the asphalt, crying.

lines.japanese: 「うぇーん、ひっ、ひっく……」
lines.english: “Waaah… Hic, hic…”

lines.japanese: 冬はいちばん転びたくない季節。どんな痛みだって倍になる。
lines.english: Winter was the worst season for falling down. Every hurt felt twice as sharp.

lines.japanese: 「だいじょうぶ？」
lines.english: “Are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 僕は車道を渡り、女の子のそばで身を屈めた。
lines.english: I crossed the road and crouched beside her.
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 「おかあさんは？」
lines.english: “Where’s your mother?”

lines.japanese: 聞きながら、少女の冷たい手を掴んだ。
lines.english: As I asked, I took her cold hand.

lines.japanese: 彼女は黙って僕の目をまっすぐ見詰めかえしながら、おとなの力に引かれてゆっくり立ちあがった。
lines.english: She looked straight into my eyes without a word and slowly rose as an adult’s strength pulled her to her feet.

lines.japanese: 剥き出しの膝に、真っ赤な血が痛々しく滲んでいた。小さな手の甲で涙を拭っている姿に、ふと、いつかの小鳩が重なった。
lines.english: Bright red blood welled painfully on her bare knee. As she wiped her tears with the back of one tiny hand, for a moment I saw Kobato as she had once been.

lines.japanese: 「うん、偉いぞー。泣かない泣かない」
lines.english: “There you go. What a brave girl. No more tears.”

lines.japanese: 僕は幼い妹をあやすように、見知らぬ女の子の黄色い帽子を撫でた。
lines.english: As though soothing my own little sister, I stroked the yellow hat of a girl I had never met.

lines.japanese: 「あ……ありが……」
lines.english: “Th… Thank…”

lines.japanese: 「しおりっ！」
lines.english: “Shiori!”

lines.japanese: 蕾みたいな唇がありがとうと花開こうとしたとき、その後ろから鋭い声を差しこまれて彼女の時間は止まった。
lines.english: Her budlike lips were just beginning to flower into a thank-you when a sharp voice thrust in from behind her, and her time stopped.

lines.japanese: 幸せな家庭を具現化したようなぴかぴかの新築の陰から、若い女性が自転車をほっぽって飛びだしてきた。
lines.english: From behind a gleaming new house that looked like happiness in domestic form, a young woman abandoned her bicycle and came flying toward us.

lines.japanese: 「何してるの、しおり！　勝手に先行っちゃ駄目でしょ！」
lines.english: “What are you doing, Shiori? You can’t just run off ahead by yourself!”

lines.japanese: 風見ヶ丘のヤングミセスは、愛娘と見知らぬ男子学生とのあいだへ滑りこむように割って入った。
lines.english: The young mother of Kazamigaoka slid between her beloved daughter and the strange schoolboy.

lines.japanese: 「あ、えっと……」
lines.english: “Oh, um…”

lines.japanese: 「膝、擦りむいちゃったみたいですね……」
lines.english: “It looks like she scraped her knee…”

lines.japanese: 僕は眉を下げて申しわけ程度に笑った。若い母親は笑わなかった。
lines.english: I lowered my brows and offered a token smile. The young mother did not return it.

lines.japanese: 「……ありがとうございます。お世話さまでした」
lines.english: “…Thank you. That was very kind.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は子供の背中を押して、逃げるように自転車置き場へ消えた。
lines.english: With one hand at the child’s back, she hurried away toward the bicycle racks as though escaping.

lines.japanese: 「しおり！　知らない男のひととお話しちゃ駄目って、いつも言ってるでしょ！」
lines.english: “Shiori! I’m always telling you not to talk to strange men!”

lines.japanese: 「うええ、でもぉ……」
lines.english: “Waaah, but…”

lines.japanese: 「でもじゃないの、謝りなさい！」
lines.english: “No buts. Apologize!”

lines.japanese: 清冽に澄んだ朝を台無しにするヒステリックな声が、ふたたび歩きはじめた僕の背中にまで届いた。
lines.english: The hysterical voice, spoiling the crystalline morning, reached my back even after I began walking again.

lines.japanese: 泣きっ面を蜂に刺されてしまった小さな心を想うと、つい戻ってひと言口を挟みたくなった。
lines.english: Thinking of that little heart—already in tears, and now stung again—I nearly turned back to put in a word.

lines.japanese: だけど１２月の白い空がしめやかに事なかれ主義を謳っているから、僕はただ馬鹿みたいに上を向いて先を急いだ。
lines.english: But the white December sky was solemnly singing the virtues of leaving well enough alone, so I merely stared stupidly upward and hurried on.

lines.japanese: ごめん、嘘かも。たぶん空は関係ない。
lines.english: Sorry. That may have been a lie. The sky probably had nothing to do with it.

lines.japanese: 僕はしばらく道の端を歩いていた。
lines.english: For a while I walked along the edge of the road.

lines.japanese: 塀や壁に一辺でも守られていないと、なんとなく落ちつかない。こんな気持ちは他のみんなも持ってるんだろうか。
lines.english: Unless a wall or fence protected me on at least one side, I never quite felt at ease. Did everyone feel this way?

lines.japanese: ことん──
lines.english: Clack—

lines.japanese: ──小さな音がした。その音がなんとなく耳について、僕はそっちの方に視線を流してみた。
lines.english: —a small sound. Something about it caught at my ear, and I let my gaze drift toward it.

lines.japanese: いつも何気なく通りすぎている、先鋭的な住宅街の中の前時代的な煙草屋。そのガラス張りの小さな窓口に僕と同学年の女子が座っていて、携帯電話を耳にあてたままぼそぼそ唇を動かしていた。
lines.english: The old-fashioned tobacco shop I passed every day without a thought, an anachronism amid the cutting-edge homes. At its little glass-fronted counter sat a girl in my year, a cell phone to her ear, her lips moving in a murmur.

lines.japanese: だいぶ小さな声だろうけど、ちゃんと相手に届いてるのかな──
lines.english: Her voice must have been terribly quiet. Could the person on the other end even hear her?

lines.japanese: ──そんなふうに思ったけれど、最近の携帯電話はそういうものなのかもしれない。通話手段として使う機会がほとんどない僕には関係のない話だ。
lines.english: Then again, perhaps that was simply how modern cell phones worked. It had nothing to do with me; I almost never used mine to make calls.

lines.japanese: 彼女の顔に、僕は覚えがあった。同じ教室で、僕のふたつ前の席に座っている山科京さん。
lines.english: I recognized her face. Miyako Yamashina, who sat two seats ahead of me in our classroom.

lines.japanese: でも知っているのは、顔と名前と、病気がちでよく学校を休んでいること。あとはせいぜい、もの静かな感じのひとってことくらい。
lines.english: All I knew was her face, her name, and the fact that poor health often kept her home from school. Beyond that, only that she seemed a quiet sort of person.

lines.japanese: 実は、必要最低限の事務的な会話しか交わしたことがなかった──僕にとって、ほとんどのクラスメイトがそうであるように。
lines.english: In truth, we had spoken only when some practical matter required it—as was the case with most of my classmates.

lines.japanese: 通話中の彼女が一瞬だけ僕を見た、ような気がした。なんとなく気まずさを感じながら、同級のよしみ程度に軽く頭を下げてみる。
lines.english: For an instant, I thought she glanced at me during her call. Feeling vaguely awkward, I gave her a small bow in acknowledgment of our being classmates.

lines.japanese: だけどやっぱり電話に夢中みたいで、もう彼女の瞳がこちらへ向くことはなかった。
lines.english: But she seemed absorbed in the call after all, and her eyes never turned my way again.

lines.japanese: 山科さんは携帯電話をたたむと同時に、すぐさま店の奥へ引っこんだ。やっぱり僕の姿に気付いたわけじゃなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: The instant Yamashina snapped her phone shut, she withdrew into the back of the shop. Apparently she had not noticed me after all.

lines.japanese: 三歩うしろに下がり、改めて煙草屋の全容を眺めてみる。ここって彼女の家だったんだ。ずっと通ってる道だけど知らなかった。
lines.english: I took three steps backward and looked over the tobacco shop properly. So this was her house. I had walked this road for years without ever knowing.

lines.japanese: これまで馴染みの通学路にクラスメイトの家があったなんて知らなかったけど、そういうのが分かるとわけもなく嬉しい。僕はかすかに微笑んで、白い朝に相応しくない軽やかな速度で歩きだした。
lines.english: I had never known a classmate’s home stood along this familiar route. Discovering it made me happy for no reason I could name. A faint smile on my lips, I set off at a buoyant pace quite unsuited to the white morning.

lines.japanese: 今日はいい天気だ。
lines.english: It was a beautiful day.

lines.japanese: 駅に着いたあと、電車待ちの退屈な数分間をもてあまして、僕は携帯電話のメモ帳に無謀な一行を付けくわえた。
lines.english: At the station, with several dull minutes to fill before my train, I added one reckless line to the notepad on my phone.

lines.japanese: “６：クラスに友達をつくる”
lines.english: “6. Make a friend in class.”
